main_text.p: æqualia veniunt arma, si mo-do iis vel mutilari vel occidi quis possit. Ut licite etiam quibuscunque armis aggressor interimatur. Ita, exempli gratia[?], qui fuste quem aggreditur, gladio munitum, eum in vitae discrimen adducere poterit, ut aggressus gladio vim atque injuriam merito propulset. Ita Hercules alter, vel pugno, baculo munitum necaret, ut jure inaequalibus armis homini robusto quis resistat. Sic enim ferunt quendam fuisse Perusinum, qui pugno in capite non tantum homines sed & boves necabat, ut tutum non satis esset ipsius ictus aut alapas experiri. Martin. Hamcon. de Rebus Geft.Frif. libr.2.Etiam Jotzardum Frisonem equum suum pugno occidisse historiis Frisiae proditum est.
l.Provi-dendum. Cod. de Postulan-do.Neque obstat ꝛ[?].Quod æqua-lis utrinque debeat esse defensio, lege ita postulante. Neque enim

page.notes: The first paragraph's opening line and the three left-margin notes are: "Cod.l. Cornel. de Sicar," beside the opening lines, which I have included as a note at the start of the text; "Martin. Hamcon. de Rebus Geft.Frif. libr.2." beside "riri. Etiam"; and "l.Provi-dendum. Cod. de Postulan-do." beside "Neque obstat". The first note is printed beside the opening line of the page, so it should be checked: I have placed it at the start of the first paragraph (the "Cod.l. Cornel. de Sicar," note is set in the margin at the top, to the left of "æqualia"). The paragraph-opening mark "ꝛ" before ".Quod" is doubtful. "gratia" is partly garbled in the scan ("g'a ia"). The catchword "enini" is doubtful. A stray dot in the left margin near "pugno" is not text and is ignored. Printed page furniture: page number 148 and running head P. VOET.
